mainText:
Good morning, it's Saturday, Sept. 12,

CIA releases intelligence sent to White House before 9/11.
The CIA yesterday released 69 never-before-seen briefs (
download here
) warning about Osama bin Laden and al-Qaida, including one warning then-President Bill Clinton about a potential plot to "fly an explosive-packed airplane into a US city.” Experts say the documents reaffirm that the US failed to respond to several warnings in the years leading up to 9/11.
US inflation accelerates and diesel prices spike as war in Iran continues.
The inflation rose 3.4% in August compared with a year ago, unchanged from July and in line with analysts’ expectations. Interest-rate futures forecast about an 85% chance the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week, up from roughly 70% before the report. Meanwhile, diesel prices hit record highs above $6 a gallon, which is expected to hike the cost of shipping groceries and other goods.
Iran-backed Houthis capture Red Sea island on vital oil shipping route.
The Houthi militia yesterday seized a Yemeni island at the choke point in the Red Sea, one day after taking control of a key Yemeni port. The moves tighten Iran and its allies' control of the Bab el-Mandab Strait, a vital oil shipping route. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia shut down a major oil pipeline after a drone attack it claims originated in Iraq. The Iraqi government has ordered an investigation.
Afghan woman deported in first-ever "alien terrorist" court case.
Nazira Haji Zada, a 47-year-old Afghan permanent resident living in Texas, opted yesterday to leave the US rather than continue litigating accusations that she supported an Islamic State-linked plot. She was the first person to appear before the Alien Terrorist Removal Court, which was established in 1996. The court allows the government to deport noncitizens whose case details cannot be publicly disclosed for national security reasons.
CDC declares nation's largest-known cyclosporiasis outbreak over.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declared that the outbreak ended yesterday, with a total of 12,883 lab-confirmed cases across 21 states since May. Officials identified at least one source—iceberg lettuce grown by Taylor Farms in Mexico—and are investigating at least five other potential sources.
US Open wraps this weekend.
The world's new No. 1 women's tennis player, Elena Rybakina, faces the old No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in the women's final today at 4 pm ET. This is Rybakina’s first US Open final, while Sabalenka is seeking her third straight title after winning in 2024 and 2025. Ben Shelton and Alexander Zverev will play tomorrow for the men's title.
Justin Trudeau launches film and TV production company.
The former Canadian Prime Minister is launching Hope & Hard Work with his former chief of staff, Katie Telford. The company is developing adaptations of Perry Chafe's 2023 novel, "Closer by Sea"; Uzma Jalaluddin's 2025 novel "Detective Aunty"; and more. Former President Barack Obama and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton both also started production companies after leaving office.
